model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms when using the Mistralv0.2-Base model, either in its base form or after being fine-tuned on specific medical specialties. The vertical axis represents “Negative log probability,” ranging from approximately -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher model confidence (i.e., lower uncertainty) in predicting the terms. The horizontal axis lists six medical specialties — Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics — each associated with a group of six vertical bars. These bars correspond to the model’s performance on terms from each specialty when fine-tuned on one of the six specialties (including itself), as indicated by the legend: light blue for “Mistralv0.2-Base” (unfine-tuned), and colored bars for fine-tuning on Cardio (light beige), Gastro (light orange), Infect (medium orange), Neuro (darker orange), Obstetrics (brown), and Pediatrics (dark brown). Within each specialty group, the bars are arranged from left to right in the order listed in the legend. Generally, the bar corresponding to fine-tuning on the same specialty as the test terms (e.g., “Cardio” fine-tuned on “Cardio” terms) tends to be among the lowest (most confident), while the base model (light blue) often shows higher negative log probability (lower confidence). For example, in the “Cardio” group, the base model bar is the tallest (lowest confidence), while the “Cardio” fine-tuned bar is among the shortest. Similar patterns are visible across other specialties, suggesting that fine-tuning on a specific domain improves the model’s ability to predict terms from that domain. The bars are not sorted by height within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
